raw_response:
I am on 8 mu only, and this land feeds the family, so I won't do anything fancy. Same as past years, I will keep the wheat-maize rotation. Wheat and maize together are steady for us. If one side is not so good, the other can still bring something back. I cannot read those technical things, so I do it the way I know from my own fields and what people around here do. Wheat I will sow in early October, not too late, with the village variety people usually buy. Before sowing I will put a base fertilizer, not too little because if wheat turns weak in winter and spring, yield drops badly. But I also cannot spend too much cash at once, so I will split some nitrogen and save part for spring topdressing. Water from the well costs money, but if there is no rain, wheat still needs the key irrigations.

After wheat harvest, maize must go in quickly. That turn is always rushed, so I will not do heavy tillage, just quick field cleaning and shallow preparation, then sow maize right away in mid-June. Maize usually does well after wheat here if it catches the season on time. I will use hybrid seed like most people do, apply fertilizer mostly at planting and then a little more later if the crop looks pale. If rain is normal, maybe I irrigate once; if it is dry, then twice. I do not spray unless I see a real weed or insect problem, because every bottle costs money. My thinking is simple: keep the land in the usual rotation, spend where it protects yield, and not gamble the family's cash.
